html:
Darul Uloom Deoband is an Islamic seminary founded in 1866 in the town of Deoband, north of Delhi. It gave its name to the Deobandi movement, one of the largest schools of Sunni Islam in South Asia.

It was born out of the defeat of 1857. After the Indian Rebellion the Mughal court was gone and many Muslim scholars felt Islam itself was at risk under British rule. Scholars led by Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi chose to build learning without the state: a school paid for by small public gifts, teaching the Quran, the sayings of the Prophet and Hanafi law.

Its outlook was reformist. It urged strict practice of the law and opposed customs it saw as additions, such as some rites at Sufi shrines. That set it against the rival Barelvi school. It took a different path from Aligarh, which embraced English education.

Its graduates founded thousands of madrasas across India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Britain and South Africa. In politics many Deobandi scholars backed the Congress and opposed the Partition of India. Later, some Deobandi madrasas in Pakistan schooled the leaders of the Taliban.
sum: Darul Uloom Deoband is an Islamic seminary founded in 1866 in the town of Deoband, north of Delhi. It gave its name to the Deobandi movement, one of the largest schools of Sunni Islam in South Asia.
